evals.prompt: Our CLIF lead has six site summaries, two failed logistic fits, one log-RR and five log-OR estimates, possible transfer overlap, and no adjustment dictionary. Write the R/Python synthesis plan and input checks.
evals.expected_output: Reconciles every site and blocks independent pooling until scale, estimand, overlap and model compatibility are resolved.
expectations: Keeps failed fits as unavailable with reasons rather than zero effects
Does not pool log-RR and log-OR together
Requires adjustment/estimand compatibility and an overlap assessment
Separates coefficient meta-analysis from global model fitting and returns a site reconciliation plan

evals.prompt: For our preregistered review, generate R REML and Python statsmodels code for independent adjusted log-HRs. We have four studies. Can the two engines be called equivalent and can we use Egger to prove no publication bias?
evals.expected_output: Produces explicit method guidance and declines unsupported method equivalence and bias claims.
expectations: Identifies statsmodels iterated as Paule-Mandel rather than REML
Explicitly selects HKSJ/Knapp-Hartung intervals rather than relying on defaults
Explains small-k heterogeneity and prediction interval uncertainty
Does not use Egger with four studies or interpret its result as proof of no publication bias

evals.prompt: Plan a healthcare systematic review of observational intervention studies in R. We have searched PubMed once but have no protocol, second reviewer or risk-of-bias decisions. Provide what is needed before pooling.
evals.expected_output: Provides protocol, source and reviewer workflows without fabricating completed actions.
expectations: Distinguishes PRISMA/MOOSE reporting from Cochrane conduct and statistical validity
Records prospective registration eligibility/timing and does not invent an identifier
Requires documented topic-appropriate database searches and independent decisions
Selects an appropriate risk-of-bias tool with version and outcome-level certainty assessment
